title: Four tools added: HidraNet, RaccoonLine, OffChain and Freedomia
body: HidraNet (a Tor browser) and RaccoonLine (a decentralized VPN) join the VPN page, OffChain (a self-custody wallet that can send over SMS) joins Wallets, and Freedomia (a no-KYC Visa card) joins Private payments. Each entry quotes the service's own pages, including where they contradict each other: OffChain's SMS mode keeps an encrypted copy of your keys on its server, and Freedomia's privacy policy still lists ID data.

title: SMS and eSIM and private domains pages, payment filters
body: Two new tools pages list services that say they ask for no ID: five SMS number and eSIM sellers (Crypton.sh, nadanada, simsup, MoneroSMS, sms4sats) and four private domain registrars (IncogNET, Mynymbox, Njalla, NiceVPS). Each entry quotes the service's own pages and shows the date we read them. The home page has a tools row under the platform categories, and the list now filters by cash, bank transfer or card and can hide listings under review. LNVPN is now listed as nadanada, its new name. The English text uses American spelling.

title: AceChange: card purchases paused, blocked regions corrected
body: AceChange's own pages say card and bank purchases and cash-outs are paused, with no reopening date, so it no longer shows under card payments. Its AML page lists the United States, the EEA, the United Kingdom, Russia and Belarus as blocked regions, which the listing now says. Crypto swaps run through FixedFloat and can trigger KYC case by case, so the listing moves from none to light.

title: Nonkyc.io review notice lifted
body: Nonkyc.io's own terms say it requires no personal identification or verification. We read them in an archived copy dated 19 October 2026, because the site now blocks access from France. The listing keeps France in its unavailable countries and now links the terms as its source.

title: Xnvia removed from the directory
body: Xnvia's sign-up page now says registration is limited to invited users, and access is requested by email. A listing nobody can sign up to does not help readers, so we removed it. We will list it again once registration is open.

title: 13 listings re-read against their own terms
body: We re-read the terms of 13 listings that had no source page: Uniswap, PancakeSwap, dYdX, edgeX, Hyperliquid, 1inch, DeGate, BIM Exchange, Portal Bridge, Synapse Protocol, Symbiosis, Nonkyc.io and Boltz. Each now links its source. Corrections: dYdX also bars the United Kingdom, edgeX and Hyperliquid bar the US and Ontario, Symbiosis bars the US, and BIM Exchange moves to light because its fiat services run through providers that can ask for KYC. Nonkyc.io now blocks users in France, and its no-ID claim still has no readable source.

title: New tools page: anonymous VPS
body: The tools section now has a page for VPS hosts that take an email address and crypto: rdp.monster, Njalla, BitLaunch, PrivateAlps and FlokiNET. Each entry quotes what the host says on its own site about sign-up, payment, location and refunds. Those claims are the hosts' own and we have not tested them.

title: Xnvia added to Cash and P2P
body: Xnvia is a P2P marketplace with escrow and a 1% fee per transaction. Its support center says identity verification is mandatory, so it sits near the bottom of the list. The page with its restricted countries could not be read, and the listing says so.

title: 51 platforms added: the directory now lists 105
body: Ten exchanges (Toobit, XT.com, Bitunix, HTX, Bitget, Gate, Phemex, BitMart, WEEX, CoinW), fourteen decentralized exchanges (THORChain, Raydium, KyberSwap, DODO, Meteora, Orca, Velora, CoW Swap, Curve, Jupiter, SunSwap, Matcha, BasicSwap, eigenwallet), twelve instant swaps and swap wallets (SideShift, Exolix, Godex, Houdini Swap, Swapzone, Husher, Swapuz, CypherGoat, Blockchain.com, MyEtherWallet, Zerion, SwapSpace), six bridges and aggregators (Across, Stargate, deBridge, Squid, Jumper, Rubic), five P2P markets (RoboSats, Mostro, Vexl, lnp2pBot, RetoSwap) and four Bitcoin ATM networks (Localcoin, Byte Federal, Athena Bitcoin, Bitstop). Each listing quotes what the platform's own pages say about ID and links the page. Where those pages contradict each other, the listing says so. Five of the new exchanges ask for ID before you can withdraw.

title: Phantom Cash, RedotPay and Tria added to crypto cards
body: Phantom Cash says its wallet needs no KYC, but the debit card requires identity verification, and it is open in the US except New York. RedotPay makes ID verification mandatory for every user and is closed to US residents. Tria asks for KYC after you buy your first card. The crypto cards page now lists ten cards.

title: Crypto cards get their own page and filter
body: Seven crypto cards are now listed: WaldenPay, Kripicard, Bitget Wallet Card, Bleap, KAST, Oobit and MetaMask Card. Nearly all ask for ID, and each listing quotes what the card's own pages say about it. To make room on the home page, the filters now pair swaps with bridges, and P2P markets with ATMs.

title: WaldenPay added, with a new Crypto card type
body: WaldenPay is a virtual prepaid card you top up with crypto. Its privacy policy says it collects no government ID and its countries page says signup needs only an email, but the site also mentions onboarding and eligibility checks and never says when ID is asked. We list it as Light, with the policy marked not confirmed. The top-up fee starts at 5% and falls to 3% with volume, and issuing the card costs $10. Cards are a new type in the directory.

title: Best Wallet corrected, KCEX and PrimeXBT sources added
body: Best Wallet moves from No ID to Light: its own site says to sign up with an email, and card purchases go through a third party that may ask for ID. KCEX now links its help article, which gives 30 BTC a day as the limit for basic verification and does not state the limit without it. PrimeXBT now links its help article, which gives $20,000 per 24 hours as the withdrawal limit before verification.

title: No real-money tests: method page and listings updated
body: We do not test platforms with real money. The method page no longer describes a paid test, and each listing now says where its information comes from and links the source page when we have one.

title: ATM and swap listings checked against their own pages
body: Bitcoin Depot now asks for ID at every purchase at its US kiosks, per its own press release, and Coinstar's wallet provider checks ID before you receive the coins. Mt Pelerin treats ID as optional but holds unverified purchases for 7 days. GhostSwap, SilentSwap, Rockitcoin, WizardSwap, LibertyX, Bitcoin Well, Trocador and OpenPeer now link the page that backs their listing.

title: Tool entries translated into eight languages
body: The facts on all 103 tool entries are now translated into French, Spanish, German, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Turkish and Chinese. A note still appears on a page if any entry has no translation yet.

title: Privacy hardening page
body: A new tools page covers browsers, extensions, search engines, password managers, two-factor apps and security keys, messengers, encryption, metadata cleaners and file sharing. Same entry format and sort rule as the other tool pages.

title: Tapbit and BloFin corrected, CoinEx sourced
body: Tapbit's own blog says unverified accounts can withdraw up to 2 BTC, not 10 BTC. BloFin's help center sets a Basic level limit and its terms require identity information, so it moves from None to Light. CoinEx's help center confirms the 10,000 USD daily limit without ID verification.

title: Advertise page: free for now, in exchange for a mention
body: Until we have 30 days of audience figures, a sponsored tile is free if your site mentions that DoNotKYC features you and links to donotkyc.com. We publish prices after that.

title: Two instant swaps added, volume and reputation lines removed
body: FixedFloat and ChangeNOW join the directory, each with the page of its own terms or FAQ as the source. Both ask for ID only when a swap is flagged. The "24h volume" and "Reputation" lines are gone from the listings and the API: they were not dated and partly subjective. The TikTok link is removed.

title: Proofreading pass and tools on the home page
body: Guides and API page rewritten in plainer English, the security guide loses its closing slogan in all 9 languages, and both guides now link to the matching tool pages. The home page gets a Tools section. Promotional wording and unsourced claims are removed from a few platform listings (Best Wallet, SilentSwap and some feature tags).

title: CoinJoin tools page
body: A new tools page lists Wasabi and JoinMarket with what their own sites say. It notes which services have stopped: the Wasabi coordinator in June 2024 and the archived JoinMarket repository.

title: Tools: operating systems, e-mail and aliases
body: Four more tool pages: desktop systems (Tails, Whonix, Qubes OS and more), phone systems (GrapheneOS, CalyxOS, /e/OS, LineageOS), private e-mail providers and e-mail alias services. Same entry format and same sort rule as the other tool pages.

title: Tools section: VPN, Tor, DNS, wallets and more
body: Ten new pages list the tools people use next to a no-KYC platform: VPNs, Tor and other networks, encrypted DNS, leak tests, routers, Bitcoin, hardware and Monero wallets, privacy coins and private payments. Each entry quotes the maker's own site, says what the tool asks of you and whether its code is open, and follows one sort rule. The old VPN guide now lives on the VPN page.

title: KYC claims corrected for 4 platforms
body: We compared our listings with the platforms' own policies. Changelly and StealthEX publish identity-check policies, so they no longer read "email only" or "no ID up to $700". LocalCoinSwap can ask for ID after a dispute or an alert. Bybit lets unverified accounts withdraw up to 20,000 USDT a day but asks for ID to trade. Seven listings now link the policy page they rely on.

title: Versioned API and security contact
body: The directory is now also served at /api/v1/platforms.json, one flat list with every field. A security.txt file tells researchers where to report a problem, and robots.txt names the AI crawlers that are welcome.

title: Cookie-free visit counter
body: DoNotKYC now counts visits with GoatCounter, an open-source counter with no cookies and no personal data. The privacy policy explains what it records.

title: Synapse back to active
body: synapseprotocol.com now redirects to Hypercall, the team's new product, but the Synapse bridge still works at bridge.synapseprotocol.com. The listing points there and is no longer under review.

title: How we make money, and a privacy policy
body: Two new pages explain who pays DoNotKYC (affiliate links and labelled sponsored tiles, with our advertising rules) and confirm the site collects no data about visitors.

title: Boltz under review: swaps suspended
body: Boltz suspended its swaps on 3 August 2026 and its website no longer resolves. The listing stays visible with a warning and is out of our recommendations until the service is back.

title: Synapse under review
body: synapseprotocol.com now redirects to hypercall.xyz/synapse. We are confirming the service and its address before updating the listing.

title: 1inch moved to 1inch.com
body: The listing now points to the new domain.

title: Weekly automatic check of every listing
body: Every Monday a script checks that each platform's site still answers and has not moved to another domain.

title: Side-by-side comparisons
body: 18 comparisons of platforms that do the same job, such as MEXC vs Bybit or Bisq vs Hodl Hodl.

title: Site available in 9 languages
body: English, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Turkish and Chinese.

title: New directory, one page per platform
body: Platforms are now sorted by how much identity they ask for (None, Light, Tiered), with a page each, topic pages and alternatives to exchanges that require ID. Data errors fixed for KCEX, DeGate and Boltz. Google Analytics and third-party logos removed: the site makes no request to any other service.
